zh: 已经有序时按本题约定直接输出 0。否则，每个不在正确位置上的值在排序完成前至少要参与一次交换，而一次合法交换 v、w 要求 v & w = k，这意味着 k 的每一位都必须出现在 v 中。
因此 k 必须是所有错位值按位与 A 的子掩码，k ≤ A。反过来，A 本身就在 0..n−1 内，值为 A 的元素可以当作“中转站”：它与任何错位值的按位与都恰好是 A，借助它三次交换就能交换任意两个错位值并把它放回原处。
扫描排列，对所有 arr[i] ≠ i 的值做按位与；若没有错位值，输出 0，否则输出这个按位与的结果。时间 O(n)，额外空间 O(1)。
en: If the array is already sorted, print 0 by this problem's convention. Otherwise every misplaced value must take part in at least one swap before sorting finishes, and a valid swap of v and w requires v & w = k, so every bit of k must be set in v.

Hence k must be a submask of A, the bitwise AND of all misplaced values, so k <= A. Conversely, A itself lies in 0..n-1, and the element with value A can serve as a hub: its AND with any misplaced value is exactly A, and three swaps through it exchange any two misplaced values and put the hub back.
Scan the permutation and AND together every value with arr[i] != i; if there is no misplaced value print 0, otherwise print that AND. O(n) time and O(1) extra space.

explanationEn:
## Explicit convention for already sorted input

The original statement asks for the largest non-negative k, but for a permutation that is already sorted, zero swaps are valid for every non-negative k, so mathematically there is no finite maximum. The fixed source explanation and the Python, Java, and C++ implementations all explicitly return 0, so this site adopts the convention "return 0 when already sorted"; it must not be presented as a maximum that follows naturally from the statement. The proof of the maximum below applies only to permutations that are not yet sorted.

## Algorithm

Traverse the permutation, find all values with arr[i] != i, and AND them together bit by bit. If there is no misplaced value, output 0 by the convention. Let A be the AND of the non-empty set of misplaced values; the answer is A.

## Proof of correctness

### Necessity: every feasible k is at most A

Every value v that is initially misplaced must take part in at least one swap before sorting is complete. A valid swap satisfies v&w=k, so all set bits of k appear in v. This holds for every misplaced value, so k is a submask of A, and therefore k<=A.

### Sufficiency: a pivot inside the domain can bridge and be restored

Since 0<=A<=any misplaced value<n, A itself lies in [0,n-1]; the permutation must contain a node with value A, called the pivot. Every misplaced value v satisfies v&A=A, so v and the pivot can be swapped legally. Sorting can be decomposed into swaps between misplaced values: if one of the two values a, b to be swapped is the pivot, swap directly; otherwise swap the value pairs (A,a), (A,b), (A,a) in turn. All three steps have a bitwise AND of exactly A, and the net effect only swaps a and b and puts the pivot back in its original position. So it does not matter even if the pivot is initially in its correct position; other values already in their correct positions need not take part. Fixing the misplaced positions step by step completes the sort, proving that A is feasible. Together with the upper bound, A is the largest answer.

## Complexity and independent verification

The algorithm takes O(n) time and O(1) extra space apart from input parsing. The full n<=100000 bound and the 0..n-1 permutation domain are kept. For all 5913 permutations with n=1..7, the generator builds the value graph for each k and independently determines reachability by BFS over permutation states using actual legal swaps, while also verifying the pivot swap construction step by step; the independent oracle does not use the AND-of-misplaced-values formula. The large boundary cases include sorted, reversed, and full-cycle permutations, an answer near the upper bound of 99998, and a high-bit domain cycle with a fixed pivot of 65536. When the value 0 is misplaced, any swap involving it forces k=0; the two largest values differ in only one set bit, so the largest feasible value is 99998; the high-bit domain contains 65537 and 65538, whose only common bit is 65536, and that value can connect every value in the domain.
